examples.knowledge_point: Identifying the Interior of a Set
examples.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A = \big\{ (x,y)\in\mathbb R^2 \,:\,  y^2 - 1 \leq  x , \, -2 \leq y \leq  2 \big\}.
$$

The interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\textrm{int}\,A = \big\{ (x,y)\in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, \bbox[5px, border: 1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}, \, -2 <     y <     2\big\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
examples.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $\partial A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $\partial A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041552/assets/1ca3afd22a68f2ce8b29645879967c3d130d5c19a7d529296ff129eb92693295.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\textrm{int}\, A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\textrm{int}\,A = A - \partial A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041552/assets/6e7f7a326a89c60bbc11e48d491ed05a176161881368f189aec7aad916752b64.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\textrm{int}\,A = \big\{ (x,y)\in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, \bbox[5px, border: 1px solid black]{y^2 - 1 < x}, \, -2 <     y <     2\big\}.
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2y\ge {x}^{2}}.
$$

The boundary of $A$ is given by

$$
∂A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041552/assets/0fc95ee69ce7121c0cf8ae68029b135d9667f50275227d141f1d979f85408859.png)

From the diagram, the boundary points of $A$ lie on the  parabola $-2y={x}^{2}.$ 

Therefore,  

$$
∂A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2y={x}^{2}\,}.
$$
